revision.summary: Proposed: opponent-relative aim decoding behind a flag (default off)
revision.reason: Trace analysis shows trained agents never learn the mapping from relative position to absolute aim bin; decoding aim as an offset from the bearing to the nearest opponent removes that mapping and should also remove most of the seat asymmetry
changes: Trainer controller: --aim-decoding relative (absolute default, byte-identical when off)
Paired evaluator: bind the decoding mode per model from its manifest so opponents stay unchanged
Tests: decoder mapping from both seats, absolute-mode regression, tiny CPU training smoke, evaluator binding
revision.test_plan: CPU unit and smoke tests before any admission; then the strict paired protocol versus E1024 and F1024 with secondary aim and hit readouts

decision.reviewing: Why do harder-trained candidates stall, and which variant should follow the three queued arms?
options: Hit-credit training target (reward shaping; needs owner approval)
Opponent-relative aim decoding (action representation change; permitted)
evidence: Self-play traces: agents fire on 90-100 percent of decisions but relative aim stays at chance (0.17-0.26 within one bin of 16); training sharpens an absolute west habit
Seat asymmetry: candidates win 34 percent at seat 0 vs 44 percent at seat 1 over 2816 games; the frozen objective gives every decision of a game the same 1 or 0 target
Identical Baseline2048 weights vary 4 to 19 cutoffs per 64 games across seed sets, so single-bout differences under about 10 are noise
decision.reason: Hit credit is the most direct fix but is reward shaping, which the owner's boundary forbids without approval; relative aim decoding attacks the same failure without touching rewards
decision.next_action: Helper implements relative aim decoding with per-model evaluator binding and tests on branch egocentric-aim; owner asked about hit credit; REP2048 runs as planned
